requirements.title: DIM argument type and kind restrictions
requirements.definition: X shall be integer or real, and Y shall have the same type and kind type parameter as X.

pending.DIM-X-integer-or-real: Positive source plan calls DIM with one integer pair and one exactly representable real pair. A source-control mutation changes X to LOGICAL to reach only this unnumbered argument restriction; no diagnostic facet is claimed.
pending.DIM-Y-same-type-kind-as-X: Positive source plan calls DIM with matching same-kind operands and mutates Y to a different real kind in a source-control variant; no required diagnostic facet is claimed.

requirements.oracle: Source registration only. Future fixtures use exact integer, logical, character, shape, kind, and bit-pattern observations, and use real values only where the selected operation is exact or where the standard defines an inquiry-model value. Every positive plan establishes a non-default state first, uses a conforming companion where a zero or .FALSE. result could be vacuous, and includes a feature mutation such as changing the intrinsic name, argument order, KIND, DIM, SHIFT, or BOUNDARY value. Unnumbered argument shall-restrictions are source-control restrictions only and are not promoted to diagnostic facets.

requirements.title: DIM returns the maximum of X minus Y and zero
requirements.definition: The value of DIM(X,Y) is max(X-Y,0).

pending.DIM-positive-difference: Use DIM(7,2) expecting exact integer 5; mutate argument order so the result becomes 0.
pending.DIM-zero-for-negative-difference: Use DIM(-3.0,2.0) with exactly representable real operands expecting exactly 0.0, paired with a nonzero companion DIM(2.0,-3.0) to avoid vacuity.
pending.DIM-negative-operands: Use DIM(-2,-5) expecting exact integer 3 to prove negative operands are handled by X-Y before max with zero.
